intellectual-property.lead: Patents and copyrights are governed by federal law, while Florida law protects trade secrets and offers its own trademark registration; the filing deadlines run from 3 to 6 years.
rows: Copyright lawsuits
Within 3 years after the claim accrued (17 U.S.C. § 507(b))
Patent term
20 years from the filing date of the application, subject to maintenance fees (35 U.S.C. § 154(a)(2))
Patent damages
No recovery for infringement committed more than 6 years before the lawsuit (35 U.S.C. § 286)
Trade secrets
Within 3 years after the misappropriation is discovered or should have been discovered (Fla. Stat. § 688.007)
Florida trademark registration
Lasts 5 years and can be renewed within the 6 months before it expires (Fla. Stat. § 495.071)
src: 35 U.S. Code § 286 (time limitation on patent damages)
Florida Statutes, section 688.007 (trade secrets: statute of limitations)
Florida Statutes, section 495.071 (trademark registration: duration and renewal)
faq: How long does a patent last?
A utility patent runs for 20 years from the date the application was filed in the United States, as long as the maintenance fees are paid.
How long do I have to sue for copyright infringement?
Three years after the claim accrued, under 17 U.S.C. § 507(b).
How long do I have to sue over a stolen trade secret in Florida?
Three years after the misappropriation was discovered, or should have been discovered with reasonable diligence, under section 688.007. A continuing misappropriation counts as a single claim.
Who certifies intellectual property lawyers in Florida?
The Florida Bar certifies lawyers in Intellectual Property Law after at least five years of practice, peer review and a written exam.
intellectual-property.certName: Board Certified in Intellectual Property Law

hub.what: An intellectual property lawyer protects and enforces patents, trademarks, copyrights and trade secrets, and handles licensing and infringement disputes.
hub.whenLead: Talk to an intellectual property lawyer before you launch a brand or product, share an invention, or when someone copies your work.
when: You are choosing a business or product name
You have an invention to protect
Someone is using your brand, content or code
hub.cost: Intellectual property lawyers often charge flat fees for searches and filings and hourly rates for disputes; government filing fees are extra. Ask for the fee in writing.
questions: Are you a registered patent attorney if my matter needs one?
What searches do you recommend before filing?
How do you handle infringement cases?

admiralty-maritime.lead: Maritime injury claims are governed mostly by federal law: injured seamen can sue their employer under the Jones Act, and most maritime injury claims must be filed within 3 years.
rows: Injured seamen
A seaman injured on the job may sue the employer, with a jury trial, under the Jones Act (46 U.S.C. § 30104)
Injury and death claims
Within 3 years for personal injury or death from a maritime tort (46 U.S.C. § 30106)
Limiting a vessel owner's liability
The owner must file in federal court within 6 months after a claimant gives written notice of a claim (46 U.S.C. § 30529)
Florida boating accidents
The operator must file a written report for an injury, death, disappearance or at least $2,000 of damage (Fla. Stat. § 327.301)
src: 46 U.S. Code § 30104 (Jones Act: personal injury to or death of seamen)
46 U.S. Code § 30106 (time limit for maritime torts)
Florida Statutes, section 327.301 (written reports of boating accidents)
faq: How long do I have to file a maritime injury claim?
Generally 3 years after the cause of action arose for personal injury or death from a maritime tort, under 46 U.S.C. § 30106.
What is the Jones Act?
A federal law that lets a seaman injured in the course of employment, or the family of a seaman who dies, sue the employer in a civil action with the right to a jury trial.
Do I have to report a boating accident in Florida?

Yes, when it causes injury, death or a disappearance, or at least $2,000 of damage: the operator must send a written report to the Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission within the federal time limits.
Who certifies maritime lawyers in Florida?
The Florida Bar certifies lawyers in Admiralty and Maritime Law after at least five years of practice, peer review and a written exam.
admiralty-maritime.certName: Board Certified in Admiralty and Maritime Law

hub.what: A maritime lawyer handles legal matters on navigable waters: injuries to seamen and passengers, boating accidents, cargo and vessel disputes, and claims against ship owners.
matters: Jones Act claims for injured seamen
hub.whenLead: Contact a maritime lawyer soon after an injury at sea or a vessel accident, because federal deadlines apply and cruise tickets often set shorter ones.
when: You were injured working on a vessel
You were hurt on a cruise ship
A boating accident caused injury or damage
A vessel owner filed to limit liability
hub.cost: Maritime injury lawyers often work on contingency; commercial maritime disputes are usually billed by the hour. A contingent fee agreement must be in writing and state the percentage the lawyer receives (Rule 4-1.5(f)).
questions: How many Jones Act or cruise cases have you handled?
Which deadlines apply to my claim?
Do you take cases to trial in federal court?

health-law.lead: Florida health law regulates how providers are licensed, paid and referred patients: kickbacks and patient brokering are prohibited, and every clinic location needs its own state license.
rows: Kickbacks
Health care providers may not offer, pay, solicit or receive kickbacks for referring patients (Fla. Stat. § 456.054)
Patient brokering
Paying or receiving anything to induce patient referrals is a third-degree felony with a $50,000 fine (§ 817.505)
Clinic licensing
Each clinic location must be licensed separately by the Agency for Health Care Administration (§ 400.991)
Patient records
Practitioners must furnish copies of a patient's reports and records on request, in a timely manner (§ 456.057)
Hospital records
Licensed facilities furnish copies of patient records on written request after discharge (§ 395.3025)
faq: Is it legal to pay for patient referrals in Florida?

No. Section 456.054 bars kickbacks for referrals, and under section 817.505 paying or receiving anything to induce a referral is patient brokering, a third-degree felony with a $50,000 fine, subject to the exceptions listed in the statute.
Does a medical clinic need a license in Florida?
Yes, unless it falls under an exemption: each clinic location needs its own license from the Agency for Health Care Administration.
How do I get copies of my medical records in Florida?
Ask the practitioner, who must furnish copies in a timely manner under section 456.057; a hospital furnishes copies on written request after discharge under section 395.3025.
Who certifies health lawyers in Florida?
The Florida Bar certifies lawyers in Health Law after at least five years of practice, peer review and a written exam.

hub.what: A health care lawyer advises doctors, clinics, hospitals and other providers on licensing, regulatory compliance, billing, contracts and disciplinary matters.
hub.whenLead: Use a health care lawyer before opening or buying a practice, before entering a referral or marketing arrangement, and as soon as you receive an audit or licensing complaint.
when: You are opening, buying or selling a practice
A payer or agency opened an audit
You received a complaint against your license
You plan a marketing or referral arrangement
hub.cost: Health care lawyers usually bill by the hour, and some offer flat fees for licensing or compliance projects. Ask for an estimate in writing.
questions: Do you represent providers like my practice?
Have you handled audits or license cases with this agency?
